title: Generate an SDDC LCM support bundle exactly once across a retry
prompt:
Implement `src/vcf_sddc_lcm/client.py` as a standard-library-only Python 3.11 package client for VMware Cloud Foundation SDDC LCM 9.1. Do not add dependencies or edit any other file.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection derived directly from `specifications/sddc-lcm/sddc-lcm-openapi.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable commit `c3f3b52c845dd967cabbc21680e893292077d5ba`. Its provenance is repeated in `docs/official_sources.json`; no rendered documentation page is a contract source. Use exactly the operationIds `getTasks`, `generateComponentSupportBundle`, `getTask`, and `getComponentSupportBundles`, and do not call any other route.

Keep the supplied public API:

- `SddcLcmClient(base_url, access_token, *, timeout=10.0)`
- `SddcLcmClient.ensure_support_bundle(component_id, correlation_id, *, look_back_window=None, page_size=50) -> dict[str, object]`
- `SddcLcmError`, raised for invalid input, transport/HTTP failure, or malformed/inconsistent responses.

Generating a support bundle mutates the component, and the specification defines no idempotency-key parameter. The specified `X-Correlation-Id` request header is echoed back as `TaskSummary.correlationId` and `Task.correlationId`, so a previous attempt whose response was lost is discoverable. `ensure_support_bundle` must therefore reconcile before it mutates, and calling it twice with the same `correlation_id` must not produce a second bundle.

First page through `getTasks` filtered by `type=SUPPORT_BUNDLE`, `resourceId=<component_id>`, and `resourceType=COMPONENT`. Page zero omits `pageNumber`; each later page sends `pageNumber` derived as the previous `pageMetadata.pageNumber + 1`. Require an object response with a list `elements` and object `pageMetadata`; integer, non-boolean, nonnegative `pageNumber`, `pageSize`, `totalElements`, and `totalPages`; the requested page and page size echoed back; and no overfull or non-progressing page. `totalPages` must be at least one, the echoed page must be below it, and `totalElements` and `totalPages` must stay constant across pages. Every non-last page must contain at least one element. Stop only upon reaching the advertised last page, not merely because the accumulated element count reaches `totalElements`. Stop at the first element whose `correlationId` equals `correlation_id`. Every task summary must carry the specification-required nonblank string `id`.

If a prior task exists, adopt its `id`, report `created` as `False`, and do not call `generateComponentSupportBundle` at all. Otherwise call it exactly once with the correlation ID in the `X-Correlation-Id` header and report `created` as `True`. Then resolve the task with `getTask`: require the returned `id` to match, `correlationId` to match, and `status` to be one of the specified `TaskStatus` values `PENDING`, `SCHEDULED`, `RUNNING`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED`, failing unless it is `SUCCEEDED`. Read the bundle identifier from the task's `additionalDetails.supportBundleId`, then call `getComponentSupportBundles` and select exactly the one listed bundle whose `id` equals it.

Return a new dictionary containing exactly `taskId`, `correlationId`, `status`, `created`, and `supportBundle`, in that order. `supportBundle` must be a new dictionary containing exactly `id`, `createdTimestamp`, `size`, `name`, and `url`, in that order, preserving a missing optional member as `None`. Raise `SddcLcmError` for a blank `base_url`, `access_token`, `component_id`, or `correlation_id`, a nonpositive `timeout`, a `look_back_window` that is not an integer of at least 1, and a `page_size` outside 1 through 50.

Honor the exact wire contract. Send one `Authorization: Bearer ...` and one `Accept: application/json` header on every request. `getTasks`, `getTask`, and `getComponentSupportBundles` are bodyless GETs that must omit `Content-Type`; none of them declares the `X-Correlation-Id` header parameter, so none may send it. `getTask` and `getComponentSupportBundles` carry no query at all. The `getTasks` query order is specification declaration order: `type`, `resourceId`, `resourceType`, `pageNumber` when present, then `pageSize`. Omit every unset optional `getTasks` member: `status`, `createdBy`, `name`, `description`, `startTimeGt`, `startTimeLt`, `updateTimeGt`, `updateTimeLt`, `endTimeGt`, `endTimeLt`, and `includeSystemTasks` (including the schema default `false`). `generateComponentSupportBundle` is a POST with no query, `Content-Type: application/json`, and exactly one nonblank `X-Correlation-Id`; when `look_back_window` is unset its body is exactly `{}`, and when set it is exactly `{"lookBackWindow":<n>}`. Omission means absent, never blank, zero, false, null, an empty object, or a bare query delimiter.

Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`. The protected verifier creates runtime-only credentials, component IDs, and decoy tasks, starts the contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, and reads its flushed JSONL request log. The mock derives its only callable routes from the operationIds in `docs/contract.json` and rejects a repeated correlation ID. Verification asserts the exact sixteen-request sequence, raw targets, query member sets and ordering, header multiplicity, body bytes, that the retry adopts the existing task without mutating, that exactly two bundles exist across three calls, omission of every unset optional field, and malformed-response handling through additional loopback cases. It never contacts a live VMware endpoint.
scenario: A support-bundle generation whose response may have been lost is reconciled by correlation ID through paged getTasks before the mutating POST is issued, so a repeated call adopts the existing task instead of generating a second bundle.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves reconcile-before-mutate ordering, a single generate call per correlation ID, and omission of every unset optional field.
